title: Turlu Turlu
subtitle: Turkish roasted mixed vegetables in a tomato sauce
excerpt: A generous tray of summer vegetables roasted in olive oil and baked in a light tomato sauce. Eat warm or at room temperature with bread to scoop it up.
sourceNotes: Turkish home cooking classic. Turlu turlu translates loosely as mix mix. Every region has its own version depending on the season.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps well in the fridge for up to 3 days. The flavour improves the next day.

content.text: Turlu turlu is a Turkish tray bake of whatever vegetables are in season. The key is to cut everything to a similar size so it cooks evenly. Do not crowd the tin or the vegetables will steam instead of roast.

Heat the oven to 190C. Tip all the vegetables and garlic into a large roasting tin. Drizzle over the olive oil. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Toss to coat and spread into a single layer. Use two tins if needed.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once halfway through. The edges should be starting to colour.
Mix the chopped tomatoes, tomato puree, paprika, and oregano together in a bowl. Season. Pour this sauce over the vegetables in the tin and stir gently to combine.
Return to the oven for another 25 to 30 minutes. The sauce should reduce and coat the vegetables, and the edges should be lightly caramelised.
Scatter over the chopped parsley just before serving. Eat warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The vegetables are soft and steamed rather than roasted.
items.cause: The tin was overcrowded so moisture had nowhere to escape.
items.fix: Split between two tins or roast in two batches. Vegetables need space around them to colour properly.

items.cause: The tomatoes released a lot of liquid in the oven.
items.fix: Return to the oven uncovered for a further 10 minutes to reduce the sauce, or pour off the excess liquid before serving.

items.symptom: The potatoes are still firm inside.
items.cause: They were cut too large or the oven was not hot enough.
items.fix: Cut potatoes slightly smaller than the other vegetables, as they take longer to cook through.
